column1: # Short flags admitted by a command whose path gate names a long flag of the same first letter,
# while the short flag itself is not gated.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Path gates are keyed by flag NAME, and the schema cannot say that `-d` and
# `--destination` are one option. A gate on the long spelling therefore leaves the short spelling
# ungated whatever its arity: `hugo build -d /etc/out` auto-approved while
# checks the gated name only, so it cannot see the other spelling.
# HOW THE CANDIDATES ARE PICKED. For each gated `--long` flag, the short flag spelled with its
# first letter, when the command admits it anywhere and the gate does not name it.
# IT IS A HEURISTIC, NOT A VERDICT. Many letters are a different option (`git -c` is config,
# not `--color`). Resolving a row means checking the tool's option list: gate the short spelling
# with the same role and declare it `valued`, or keep the row because it is a different flag.
# SHRINKS ONLY. `a_short_spelling_of_a_gated_long_flag_is_gated_too` fails on a candidate that is
# not listed and on a listed row that is no longer a candidate.
